summary: The audit checks the 135 graduate units, research included, GEOPHYS 201, 6 units of GEOPHYS 300, and How We Study courses in three of the four areas, letter graded unless S/NC is the only option. For breadth you choose a 12-unit secondary research project or 12 units of secondary coursework, at least 6 of them GEOPHYS lecture units at the 200 level (seminars, research and teaching units do not count). Checked by hand: the two STEM lecture courses (which count for nothing else except the two-faculty rule), two lecture courses from two Geophysics faculty, the two What We Study courses, the rest of the secondary coursework, the 3.0 GPA, two quarters as a TA, the qualifying exam, the University Oral and the dissertation.

kj9EfP4D.why: Objectives and overview. "A minimum of 135 units of graduate study at Stanford must be satisfactorily completed" is the program's minimum; the GPA is a separate rule; "Required courses ... must be lecture courses (component LEC) taken for a letter grade unless S/NC is the only option offered" is set on the How We Study course lists.

STEM is not a subject list, so the student moves the two courses in.

87ANIqcJ.why: "The Breadth Requirement can be met with either secondary research ... or secondary coursework: 1. Secondary Research Project (12 or more graded units) ... The secondary project advisor certifies completion of this requirement. 2. Secondary Coursework (12 or more graded units) ... graded (or Instructor-mandated S/NC) lecture courses at 200 or higher levels ... At least six units must come from the Department of Geophysics. The remaining courses may be chosen from courses offered by the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability ... Secondary coursework cannot be used to meet other degree requirements." The Doerr School is not a subject list, so those units are moved in. "Secondary Coursework is a program of graded (or Instructor-mandated S/NC) lecture courses": the GEOPHYS seminars (201, 300, the 385 series), field trip (214), practical training (255), teaching (299), research (400) and TGR (801, 802) are not lectures and are left out of the GEOPHYS pool.
